topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
source_evidence: Many mutual funds offer multiple share classes that all invest in the same underlying securities but that each have different sales loads and operating expenses. This means that owning a different class of the same mutual fund may result in different investment returns.
question: Misconception: Since different share classes of a mutual fund invest in the same underlying securities, they must have the same costs and returns.
answer: Different share classes of the same mutual fund can have different sales loads and operating expenses. Those differences may lead to different investment returns, even though the classes invest in the same underlying securities.
